name: Gajar ka Halwa
ingredients: 1 kg red or orange carrots (preferably winter-harvested), finely grated
1 liter full-fat buffalo or cow milk
½ teaspoon green cardamom powder (freshly ground from pods)
¼ cup chopped almonds (blanched and slivered)
¼ cup chopped pistachios (blanched and slivered)
½ teaspoon saffron strands (optional, soaked in 2 tbsp warm milk)
2 tablespoons khoya (mawa, reduced milk solids) or full-fat milk powder (optional, for richness)
instructions: 1. In a heavy-bottomed pan, heat 2 tablespoons of ghee over medium heat. Add the grated carrots and sauté for 5-6 minutes until they soften and release their aroma.
2. Pour in the milk and bring to a gentle boil. Reduce heat to low and cook, stirring occasionally, until the milk is almost completely absorbed by the carrots. This takes about 30-40 minutes.
3. Once the milk has reduced and the carrots are tender, add the remaining ghee. Cook for another 5-7 minutes, stirring continuously, until the mixture starts to brown and caramelize slightly.
4. Add the sugar and mix well. The halwa will become liquid again; continue stirring on medium heat until the sugar dissolves and the mixture thickens, about 10-12 minutes.
5. Add the cardamom powder, saffron milk (if using), khoya or milk powder (if using), and mix thoroughly. Cook for 2 more minutes.
6. Fold in the chopped almonds, pistachios, and raisins. Reserve some for garnishing.
7. Serve warm, garnished with remaining nuts and a dollop of fresh cream if desired.
description: A golden, spiced symphony of slow-caramelized carrots, ghee, and sweet cardamom, melting into a rich, velvety halwa that whispers of Punjab's winter hearths.
